insights.text: YouTube and TikTok both finished around 30% short of planned impressions, but for unrelated reasons. YouTube spent 98% of its budget and still delivered only 72% of planned impressions because its CPM averaged 10.90 against 8.00 in the plan, 36% higher. TikTok's CPM was close to plan at 4.05 against 4.00; it fell short because only 71% of its budget was spent. The YouTube gap is a forecasting question about whether the planned price was achievable in the period, while TikTok's is a delivery question about why budget was not taken up, so the two need different owners.
alternatives_considered: late flight start on TikTok (no date data to check)
insights.causal_evidence: Arithmetic identity: impressions = spend / CPM x 1000, so with spend on plan the impression shortfall is fully accounted for by CPM.
